chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Ṣafwān, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who needs wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) while he is unable to obtain water, then he finds enough water for wudu (ablution) being sold for one hundred dirhams or one thousand dirhams, and he does possess that amount. Should he buy it and perform wudu (ablution), or perform tayammum? He said: “No, rather he should buy it. Something like this happened to me, so I bought it and performed wudu (ablution), and what is bought for that is not a great amount of wealth.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), for which purification is being sought
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution) required for ritual purity before salat (prayer)
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a unit of money indicating the financial cost of obtaining water
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: to perform tayammum in place of water purification
key_terms.يَشْتَرِي: to purchase the water despite its price

ai.seo_question: If water for wudu is available only at a very high price, should one buy it or perform tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on one who needs wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) and can only obtain water at a high price. The Imam عليه السلام rules that if he possesses the money, he should buy the water and perform wudu (ablution) rather than resort to tayammum, indicating that such an expense does not excuse abandoning water purification.
